clue.text: All those tags with which we are familiar on the city pages?

definitions.text: All those tags with which we are familiar on the city pages?

parts.words: All those tags with which we are familiar on the city pages?
parts.note: tags are familiar quoted sayings, and 'familiar' ones are stock phrases; on a newspaper's City (financial) pages the phrase means listed share prices

explanation.surface: A remark about the well-worn phrases that fill a newspaper's financial section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tags' looks like labels, but it means quotations, and 'those with which we are familiar' are stock ones; the City is London's financial district, whose pages list share prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Share prices printed in the financial press are the listed values of company securities, read as 'stock' plus 'quotations'.

clue.text: Its recipient is greeted with rising enthusiasm

definitions.text: Its recipient is greeted with rising enthusiasm

parts.words: Its recipient is greeted with rising enthusiasm
parts.note: 'rising' is literal: the audience gets to its feet to applaud a performer

explanation.surface: Someone receives a welcome that grows ever warmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' seems to mean growing, but the audience literally rise from their seats.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience applauding while on its feet is the highest acclaim a performer can receive.

clue.text: Fringe defence for open-air employment?

definitions.meaning: a fortification built beyond the main defensive line
read as two words, work done outside

explanation.surface: Asks whether guarding the edges counts as a job done outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Military fortifications outside the main walls carry this name, and read as 'out' plus 'work' it means labour done outdoors.

clue.text: A piece of clinker by the roadside

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lump of furnace slag lying at the edge of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised edge of a pavement runs along the side of the road.

clue.text: Slip out of gear

parts.note: read as taking off one's clothes ('gear'), not a car's gears disengaging

explanation.surface: A car's transmission jumping into neutral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gear' suggests a gearbox; here it is clothing, and to slip out of it is to take it off.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing one's clothes is to strip, and 'gear' is informal for clothes.

clue.text: Comparatively pungent place in Morocco?

definitions.meaning: a port city on the Strait of Gibraltar

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Moroccan town has the stronger smell.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of a word for sharp-tasting is spelt the same as the Moroccan port city.

clue.text: Sporting way to decide who will have first use of pitch maybe

definitions.text: Sporting way to decide who will have first use of pitch maybe

parts.words: Sporting way to decide who will have first use of pitch maybe
parts.note: before a cricket match the captains flip a coin to decide who bats first on the pitch

explanation.surface: How teams settle who plays first on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the captains flip a coin before play and the winner chooses whether to bat or bowl first.
explanation.definitionFit: Flipping a coin is the fair, chance-based method sports use to choose ends or batting order.

clue.text: Horace Walpole's down-at-heel Italian castle

parts.note: Walpole wrote the Gothic novel about a castle in a town that sits down at the heel of Italy's boot

explanation.surface: A shabby, decaying castle from an eighteenth-century novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down-at-heel' means shabby, but here it places the town down in the heel of Italy, in Apulia; Walpole's 1764 novel is The Castle of ___.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apulian town in Italy's heel is the setting and title of Walpole's Gothic novel.

clue.text: A flash of heavenly warmth?

parts.note: a flash in the sky during the hot season, read as warmth from the heavens

explanation.surface: A sudden burst of divine affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly warmth' sounds spiritual; it is the hot season's sky, and the flash is sheet lightning seen on warm evenings.
explanation.definitionFit: Distant sheet lightning without thunder, seen on warm nights, is named after the hottest season.

clue.text: Weary at first, but ready to appear in public

indicators.note: 'at first' says the word at is placed at the front, before the synonym

parts.note: weary means tired

explanation.surface: Someone exhausted but dressed and set to go out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' reads as 'initially'; it puts AT in front of TIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed means clothed and so fit to be seen in public.

clue.text: Holy man in no spirit for a quack remedy

indicators.note: the holy man is placed in the phrase for no spirit

parts.note: rum is a spirit, so no spirit is NO RUM
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A teetotal saint offered a dubious cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A patent medicine of doubtful worth peddled by a charlatan is this; also any pet scheme.

clue.text: A little prod, it could be

indicators.note: says the word prod could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A small nudge, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A small amount of liquid is a tiny quantity, as in 'just a little'.

clue.text: Lived to return to Satan

indicators.note: to return means the word lived is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone survived only to go back to the Devil.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief evil spirit of Christian belief is named both ways.

clue.text: A note deciphered before?

indicators.note: a cipher is an old word for zero, so de-ciphered means the O-shaped zero is taken out of a note

explanation.surface: A coded message decoded ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deciphered' seems to mean decoded; read it as de-cipher, removing the cipher (zero, O) from A NOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin prefix meaning prior to, as in antenatal, also stands alone for 'before'.

clue.text: A fish that is silvery-grey or brown in colour

definitions.meaning: the grayling, a silvery freshwater fish, has this old name
a brown earth pigment used by painters

explanation.surface: Describes a fish whose scales are either grey or brown.
explanation.definitionFit: The grayling is also called by the name of the brown earth pigment.

clue.text: Large antelope put on a cross

parts.note: to add is to put on
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A big antelope nailed to a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale North African desert antelope with spiral horns.

clue.text: Kimonos specially ordered for a character in Hiawatha

indicators.note: the letters of kimonos are put in a special new order

explanation.surface: Japanese robes custom-made for an actor in a Longfellow play.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiawatha's grandmother in Longfellow's poem bears this name.

clue.text: The ginger-nut bird?

parts.note: 'nut' is the head and 'ginger' its red colour: a finch with a red crown

explanation.surface: A biscuit-loving bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ginger-nut' looks like the biscuit; read it as a red head ('poll' is an old word for head).
explanation.definitionFit: A small finch with a red forehead patch, named for its red head.

clue.text: Bribe lavishly, the sheikh can, if he has one!

definitions.meaning: to oil is to bribe (grease the palm), done well

definitions.text: the sheikh can, if he has one!
definitions.meaning: a shaft drilled for petroleum, which makes a sheikh rich enough to bribe

explanation.surface: A rich sheikh can afford to grease palms generously.
explanation.definitionFit: To grease palms thoroughly is to 'oil well', and a petroleum shaft is what makes a sheikh rich.

clue.text: Plea to be on one's guard against introspection

definitions.text: Plea to be on one's guard

definitions.meaning: looking outwards rather than in, the reverse of looking inward

explanation.surface: Advice to stay alert rather than brood.
explanation.definitionFit: A shouted 'Watch it!' warns of danger, and gazing outward is the opposite of looking within.

clue.text: Innocent young skipper going over the new archbishop's palace

indicators.note: the young animal goes over, ahead of, the next piece

parts.note: a young sheep skips and is a byword for innocence

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of the are made anew

explanation.surface: An innocent young boat captain going aboard to meet a newly appointed archbishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skipper' suggests a captain; it is a frisking young sheep. The palace is the London residence of the Archbishop of Canterbury.
explanation.definitionFit: The Archbishop of Canterbury's official London residence is a palace on the Thames.

clue.text: Regardless of others, he ruthlessly steers a middle course

definitions.text: Regardless of others, he ruthlessly steers a middle course

parts.words: Regardless of others, he ruthlessly steers a middle course
parts.note: the middle course is literally the centre of the road, which a selfish motorist hogs

explanation.surface: A ruthless politician pursuing moderate policies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steers a middle course' sounds like political compromise; it is a driver keeping to the centre of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfish motorist who drives down the centre and blocks others.

clue.text: A savoury piece of scarce coinage?

definitions.meaning: cheese on toast, served as a savoury course
read as two words, an uncommon coin

explanation.surface: Asks whether a tasty snack is a rare coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh cheese on toast is spelt the same as 'rare' (scarce) plus 'bit' (a coin).

clue.text: He broke through every restraint with spectacular sue- V cess

definitions.text: He broke through every restraint with spectacular sue- V cess

parts.words: He broke through every restraint with spectacular sue- V cess
parts.note: an escapologist who freed himself from handcuffs, chains and locked tanks

explanation.surface: Someone who overcame every limit and triumphed.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'restraint' literally: chains, cuffs and straitjackets, from which the famous escapologist freed himself on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hungarian-American escapologist was famed for freeing himself from shackles and locked containers.

clue.text: Frenzied reply telegraphed to an anxious inquirer

definitions.text: Frenzied reply telegraphed to an anxious inquirer

parts.words: Frenzied reply telegraphed to an anxious inquirer
parts.note: a terse telegram reply to someone worried about you, words run together to save cost

explanation.surface: A frantic answer wired to a worried relative.
explanation.walkthrough: Telegrams were charged by the word, so 'I am OK' becomes two words run together, which also spell a word for frenzied.
explanation.definitionFit: Running wild in a frenzy, a word from Malay, which also reads as 'am OK'.

clue.text: The card-game British Rail ring me about

parts.note: a ring is O-shaped

indicators.note: me goes about, around, British Rail

parts.note: BR is the abbreviation for British Rail, the former UK national railway

explanation.surface: Someone invited by the railway company for a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A seventeenth-century Spanish trick-taking card game for three players.

clue.text: Go on green

parts.note: a 'go' is a turn, taken on a golf green, not a traffic signal

explanation.surface: A traffic-light instruction to drive off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go on green' sounds like traffic lights; a 'go' here is a golfer's turn on the putting green.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle golf stroke made on the putting surface to roll the ball to the hole.

clue.text: Female wear that wasn't long in fashion

definitions.text: Female wear that wasn't long in fashion

parts.words: Female wear that wasn't long in fashion
parts.note: 'wasn't long' is literal: a very short skirt, popular in the 1960s

explanation.surface: A woman's garment that was a passing fad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasn't long in fashion' suggests a short-lived trend; it means the skirt itself was short.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirt ending well above the knee was the 1960s' signature short garment.

clue.text: Constructive idea

parts.note: 'constructive' read literally: a drawing for constructing a building, as well as a useful scheme

explanation.surface: A helpful suggestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constructive' means helpful but also to do with construction: an architect's drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme of action, or an architect's drawing of a building, both outline what is to be made.

clue.text: Think the world of someone that is inwardly unusually solid

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inwardly, inside the abbreviation

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of solid are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: Admiring someone who is unusually firm at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inwardly' puts DOLIS, the anagram of SOLID from 'unusually', inside IE.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship or adore someone is to regard them as a hero.

clue.text: Bad libel about fashionable Venetian artist

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about, around, the word for fashionable
bad here means the letters of libel are put wrongly, shuffled

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: A damaging slander about a trendy painter from Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts BELLI, the anagram of LIBEL from 'Bad', around IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni and his family were Renaissance painters of Venice, also remembered in a peach cocktail's name.

clue.text: Offering no resistance, nevertheless

definitions.meaning: read as three words, not resisting
a preposition or adverb meaning despite that

explanation.surface: Someone gives in, all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as 'not' plus 'withstanding' it means failing to resist, and as one word it means in spite of that.
